newsitem.title: INDIA: Eight days after India cyclone, 925 still missing.
newsitem.headline: Eight days after India cyclone, 925 still missing.

text.p: More than 900 people are still missing eight days after a cyclone lashed the southeast Indian coast, a senior state government official said on Thursday.
Chandrababu Naidu, Andhra Pradesh state's chief minister told reporters that 847 had been killed by the cyclone and 925 were still missing.
He also accused the New Delhi government of failing to release enough resources quickly to help Andhra Pradesh overcome the calamity.
The Indian Red Cross said hundreds of people in outlying villages were still cut off by flood waters following the torrential rains and flood waters driven by 180 kmph (110 mph) winds on November 6.
Helicopters have been dropping food and drinking water to the stranded villagers.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has begun deliveries of 250,000 swiss francs ($200,000) worth of aid to the area following a request for help from the Indian Red Cross.
The Swiss-based ICRC is seeking another one million swiss francs from its membership to aid the Andra Pradesh cyclone victims. ($1=1.2692 Swiss Franc)
